clue.text: Whereby dummy's not so dumb

parts.note: the dummy is a ventriloquist's doll, which seems to talk thanks to its operator's art of throwing the voice

explanation.surface: A remark that a fool, or a bridge dummy, is cleverer than they look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dummy' reads as a fool or the idle hand at bridge, but it is the doll on a performer's knee; the art that makes it speak is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing the voice so a doll appears to talk is the performer's craft, the means by which a wooden figure seems able to speak.

clue.text: They let daylight in on Rialto carousings

definitions.text: They let daylight in on Rialto carousings

parts.words: They let daylight in on Rialto carousings
parts.note: the Rialto bridge suggests a city of canals, and carousings are binges, so these are that city's drinking bouts which also adjust a window's light

explanation.surface: Revellers on the Rialto bridge partying until dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rialto is Venice's famous bridge; a 'blind' is slang for a drinking spree, so Venetian blinds are Venice's carousings and also slatted window shades.
explanation.definitionFit: Slatted window shades of this kind are tilted to admit or shut out sunlight; blind is also slang for a drinking spree.

clue.text: Without a reason to be upset by a blow in the face

indicators.note: to be upset means the letters left are tipped into a new order
without tells us the letter of the word a is left out of the word reason first

explanation.surface: Someone becoming angry for no reason at all after being punched in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without a' removes A from REASON, and 'to be upset' rearranges what is left, RESON.
explanation.definitionFit: A noser is old boxing slang for a punch on the nose, the face's most prominent feature.

clue.text: Gives America based, engineer his job again

definitions.text: Gives America based, engineer his job again

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, the British army's engineering corps
based in America is in the States

explanation.surface: A firm taking back an engineer who now lives in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a stock crossword engineer; 'America-based' is IN STATES. The whole clue describes taking someone back on.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore someone to a post they held before, rehiring them.

clue.text: Doctors cutting figures in a dance

explanation.surface: Surgeons operating while also cutting a fine figure on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lancers was a Victorian square dance made of several sets of moves called figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons who lance boils are lancers, and the Lancers is a quadrille danced in a sequence of figures.

clue.text: Odd-consuming a couple of litres, he settles disturbances

indicators.note: consuming means the first word eats, or contains, the second piece

parts.note: odd means queer, strange
two litres are two Ls

explanation.surface: An eccentric drinker downing two litres and calming a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: One who quells puts down unrest, subduing riots or quarrels.

clue.text: Girl 'who upset Tsar in Indian city

indicators.note: upset in a down light means the letters are turned upside down, read from the bottom
in says the word tsar sits in the city name, so taking it away leaves the rest

parts.note: Amritsar is a city in the Punjab, India
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman who unsettled a Russian emperor visiting India.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove TSAR from AMRITSAR to leave AMRI; 'upset' turns that to read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Irma is a female first name, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: One thousand souls in torment-all Fascist

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: torment suggests twisting and racking, so these letters are tortured into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A thousand lost souls suffering under a Fascist regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torment' scrambles SOULS into USSOL, set between M (a thousand) and IN, with I (one) last.
explanation.definitionFit: Benito Mussolini founded Italian Fascism and led the country as dictator.

clue.text: Poor fire-watcher ultimately joined by Jane at Winchester

definitions.text: Poor fire-watcher ultimately joined by Jane at Winchester

parts.words: Poor fire-watcher ultimately joined by Jane at Winchester
parts.note: a king said to have let a peasant woman's cakes burn while minding the hearth, later buried in Winchester, where the novelist Jane Austen also lies

explanation.surface: A careless air-raid warden finally meeting a woman named Jane in a Hampshire city.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says a Saxon king hiding from Danes let cakes burn; Winchester, his capital, holds his remains, and Jane Austen is buried in its cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth-century king of Wessex, buried at Winchester, is the hero of the burnt-cakes story.

clue.text: One loses nothing with learning but ignorance

indicators.note: loses tells us a letter is dropped from the word one

parts.note: taken as written, the word one
nothing is zero, the letter O
science is systematic knowledge or learning

explanation.surface: A paradox: a person who gives up nothing and gains learning ends up only ignorant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes O out of ONE, leaving NE, which is followed by SCIENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nescience is a formal word for lack of knowledge, from the Latin for not knowing.

clue.text: Flower of German wine

explanation.surface: A poetic description of a fine Rhine-region vintage as the best of its kind.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords a 'flower' is something that flows, a river: the Mosel runs through western Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mosel is a river (a thing that flows) and also the white wine made in vineyards along its valley.

clue.text: Revolutionary acts

parts.note: read not as uprisings but as rotations, and also as stage performances, the variety-show sense of an act

explanation.surface: A heading about political uprisings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests rebels; here it means going round, and 'acts' are music-hall routines.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotations are revolutions, and variety performers each do their spot on the bill, so both senses fit one word.

clue.text: The girl in Simon's room

indicators.note: in asks for what lies inside the room's name, its first and last letters dropped

parts.note: Simon the Cellarer is a Victorian comic song, so his room is the cellar

explanation.surface: A question of which young woman is in a man's bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simon the Cellarer' was a popular Victorian song; his room is the CELLAR, and 'in' takes its inside, losing the first and last letters C and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a common female name, so it serves for any young woman.

clue.text: Is it way out to do nothing right?

parts.note: the verb do, taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A slangy question whether doing nothing is the trendy, far-out thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way-out' as slang means eccentric; here it is literal, an exit.
explanation.definitionFit: A door is the usual exit from a room, the way through to the outside.

clue.text: Hard-baked aristocrats

explanation.surface: A sneer at stubborn, hidebound nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: The top crust of a loaf is the hard baked surface, and the phrase is also an idiom for the highest social class.

clue.text: Money overdue for classic art round the back

indicators.note: round means the Latin word goes around the other piece

parts.note: ars is the Latin, or classical, word for art
the rear is the back

explanation.surface: A complaint that payment for an old painting is late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classic' points to Latin, as in the tag ars longa, vita brevis; the back of something is its rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrears are sums owed that have passed their due date, payments that are behind.

clue.text: Beastly din in Hyde Park

parts.note: beastly means nasty, rotten
a row is a loud noise, a din

explanation.surface: Animals making a racket in a London park.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotten Row is the horse-riding track along the south side of Hyde Park, London.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous bridleway in Hyde Park bears this name, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: How falsely the salesman answered !

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative
speaking falsely is lying, so the salesman lied

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a dishonest salesman's reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Replied is a past-tense verb meaning responded, just as answered is.

clue.text: Beers with gin

parts.note: one word covers both a type of English ale and the flavouring added to gin, as in pink gin

explanation.surface: An order for a round of beer with gin chasers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British hoppy ale, and Angostura bitters are added to gin to make the drink called pink gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural bitter means pints of British hoppy ale, and the aromatic tincture shaken into gin has the same name.

clue.text: Singers. Italian, over Islington

parts.note: sopra is Italian for over or above
Islington in London has the postcode N1, read as NI

explanation.surface: An Italian vocal group flying over a London borough.
explanation.walkthrough: SOPRA is Italian for 'over'; Islington is the N1 postal district of north London, with the 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Soprani is the Italian plural for the highest female voices, so it names a group of vocalists.

clue.text: Nurse Darling's French aspiration ?

parts.note: cheri is French for darling, here with the possessive 's
aspiration is breathing, the sound of the letter H

explanation.surface: Wendy Darling, from Peter Pan, wishing to speak French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darling' looks like Wendy's surname; it is CHERI, French for darling, kept with its 's. An aspirate, the breathed sound, is H.
explanation.definitionFit: To cherish is to tend lovingly, just as one may nurse a hope or a patient.

clue.text: Burdensome, the cares of Henry Ford

explanation.surface: A remark on the heavy worries of a famous car maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Carking is an old word for troublesome; Henry Ford, the motor magnate, was a car king, so his cares are car-king ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Carking means oppressive or worrying, and the American motor manufacturer was a car king.

clue.text: In the lists one met with reversal

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: with reversal means the word met is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A knight at a tournament meeting an opponent and being unseated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lists' suggests a jousting ground; it means lists of entries, each entry in one.
explanation.definitionFit: Each separate entry on a list or agenda is called by this name.

clue.text: Crystalline mineral box

explanation.surface: A description of a box made of crystal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' here is the verb, to fight with fists.
explanation.definitionFit: Spar is a glassy crystalline rock such as feldspar, and to spar is to box in practice.

clue.text: Chieftain's followers-note the ring of steel

parts.note: a Highland chief's followers are his clan
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A Scottish chief's men clashing swords on the battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is the loud ringing sound of metal struck on metal.

clue.text: Omar's rousing cry

parts.note: the Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam opens with a cry to wake up, as morning has cast a stone into the bowl of night

explanation.surface: A Persian poet urging his followers to action.
explanation.walkthrough: FitzGerald's translation of the Rubaiyat begins with this exclamation, a call for the sleeper to rise.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry rouses a sleeper; as an adjective the word means not asleep.

clue.text: It includes matter from Percy's Travels

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A book review saying a work includes material from Percy's travel writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matter' suggests content of a book; it is bodily matter, pus or fluid enclosed in a sac.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyst is a sac in the body holding fluid or semi-solid substance.

clue.text: Classic style of Yankee headgear

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain hat is a timeless American style.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby at Epsom is one of the five English horse-racing Classics; in America a bowler hat is called a derby.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epsom race is one of Britain's top flat races, and Americans call the round hard felt bowler hat by that name.

clue.text: How to make tart

parts.note: reads as a recipe for pastry, but tart is the adjective, sour-tasting

explanation.surface: A heading in a baking book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like the pastry; it is the adjective, and to make something sour is to add acid to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To acidulate is to make slightly sour, for instance with lemon juice.

clue.text: A gentler twist, perhaps the old way

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of a gentler twist could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a softer turn of phrase is the traditional approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'perhaps' rearranges A GENTLER TWIST. Watling Street is the Roman road from Dover through London to Wroxeter.
explanation.definitionFit: Watling Street is an ancient Roman road in Britain, a way that is very old.
